S2 T1 dermatoid-brassy-junco IMPLEMENTED and PUSHED: Gerrit 1892, commit with Change-Id I65fb1a51, LLM-Review +1 already. binding_lifecycle.py 229 LOC new, binding_store.py 710 -> 646. Held-out validation: ALL 11 withheld discriminators passed unseen (rebind single-pop, unbind orphan sweep, keyless-entry sweep, rekey both-index swap with absence reset, lifecycle-mutates-repo-dicts, unknown-field survival, keyed-pending sub-state, and all four facade rekey fall-through cases); 3275 passed + 9 skipped across tests/unit/rebar_reconciler + tests/interfaces/store; make lint 0; typecheck 566 Success; env registry still fresh (no line shift, since _env_int did not move in this slice).
MUTATION FOUND A SECOND REAL ORACLE GAP - same pattern as S1 T2, the method working twice: 'bind_confirm SWEEPS reverse instead of one targeted pop' stayed GREEN across all 24 tests. My fixture had loc-A rebinding and only one other reverse entry which belonged to a DIFFERENT local id, so a sweep keyed on local_id and a targeted pop of the named old key were indistinguishable. Added test_bind_confirm_rebind_does_not_sweep_an_out_of_band_orphan: with a reverse key pointing at loc-A that the entry never named, the targeted pop LEAVES it and a sweep would remove it. Pinning survival is the correct characterization - it is why unbind carries a sweep and why bridge fsck reports reverse_missing_forward at all - so that test deliberately does NOT assert the one-to-one invariant. A second reported tautology was MY bad mutation, not a gap: I added an unused cached attribute, a no-op; re-run as a real aliasing break (return dict(self._repo.bindings)) it goes RED. Final: 6 mutations all RED - index copy, rebind sweep, dropped unbind sweep, keyed-pending promoted to confirmed, entry rebuilt losing unknown fields, and each half of the re-key omitted.
PROCESS: first commit attempt silently aborted with binding_store.py in MM state (staged + unstaged) because pre-commit stashed/restored around a partially-staged file; verify-commit-ticket then read the OLD HEAD and resolved RP-04's ticket 9515, and the push failed as no-new-changes. Recommitted, then confirmed the committed binding_store.py is byte-identical to the version I validated, and folded the subagent's later comment-only polish in via --amend WITH the Change-Id carried forward (the S1 T2 lesson applied - one change, not a duplicate).
COORDINATOR ADVISORY HANDLED: S2's attestation had gone stale-material purely because I added the 8th file_impact path on instruction (signed sha 47c5626f8b still an ancestor, so no base drift). sign-review correctly REFUSED (a changed plan cannot be certified from a stale PASS), so I ran a fresh review-plan brainy-cooked-hog: PASS, signed. Done at this natural break so S3's review cannot be poisoned by a stale S2 fingerprint. Adopting the ordering advice: T2 sportive-statued-goose file_impact set FIRST, BEFORE earning its attestation - 4 -> 6 paths, adding scripts/config_ownership_exceptions.py (T2 is the slice that moves note_absent and therefore _env_int and the RECONCILER_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE read, so BOTH binding_store.py registry rows must be re-registered in the same change or the pre-commit hook blocks it) and docs/adr/0099 (which already carries the forward note about this move and should record it as realized).
